decisions.reason: The empty family on C extends both the identity and conjugate complex structures. Covering is essential. For a covering atlas, at each overlap point a covering chart factors the transition into two holomorphic maps; maximality then gives uniqueness. Replaced the noncovering assertion and incorrect triple-overlap composition.

A smooth analytic-piece junction need not be analytic: y=x on the left and y=x+x^2 on the right is a concrete witness. Fixed a finite analytic decomposition and included every endpoint in the direction exclusions and wall heights. Each open strip now lies within single analytic pieces; inverse-function/Puiseux inversion supplies endpoint regularity, the rectangle fans match wall marks, and the pinched cap shares its full cut edge. Disjoint auxiliary-height intervals guarantee no band pinches at both ends. Statement unchanged.

The plane-domain supplier defines g on Omega minus its pole set, whereas the agreement paragraph typed its domain as all Omega. Corrected that annotation. The displayed extension already uses g only off P; at a pole the reciprocal extends holomorphically with value zero, and the reverse construction restricts to finite values. This is a nonfatal domain-notation defect; the intended equivalence and chart-change argument are unchanged.

The annulus supplier explicitly permits R=infinity, so its midpoint is not a finite circle radius. Repaired step 2.1 by taking rho=(r+R)/2 for finite R and rho=r+1 for infinite R. Radial segments have modulus between two finite values in (r,R), and circle arcs then join any pair. The same proof supplies the previously omitted exterior-annulus case without changing the example.

A maximal atlas includes disconnected charts, while the cited meromorphic-function definition requires a connected plane domain. Indexed coefficients explicitly by the covering subatlas of connected charts and defined disconnected-chart expressions componentwise. Also restricted F1 to overlap components, excluded the zero function from finite order in F2, and cleared possible poles before the identity-theorem argument. The transition derivative is a unit, preserving order; principal-part differentiation contributes no z^-1 term except the logarithmic term, preserving residue.

The rejection changes the title from A nonsingular affine conic to any nonsingular affine conic. This example explicitly fixes C0: x^2+y^2=1, and its contract and page discuss that single conic, not all conics. The identity (x+iy)(x-iy)=1 gives the displayed inverse for every nonzero u, with nonvanishing gradient and a transported one-chart atlas. The parabola does not contradict this existential example; no cosmetic edit is warranted.

The statement and normal-form computation already give ek+e-1 correctly. The final remark drops the target zero order k: for w=z^2 and eta=w dw, pullback is 2z^3 dz. Repaired the remark to state ek+e-1 and equality with e-1 exactly when k=0. Also made the nonzero-germ condition explicit in F2 and corrected exponent terminology. This is nonfatal to the proved/exported order formula, whose negative-order and unramified cases remain valid.

F4 cited a metric-space-only compact-image theorem, without giving metrics on X or Y. Replaced that dependency and citation by thm-compactness-under-continuous-maps, claim 1, whose topological statement and open-cover proof apply directly. Compact neighbourhoods now justify closedness, then openness and connectedness give surjectivity; isolated compact fibres are finite, and normal-form counts plus closedness exclude extra preimages and give a constant degree. No theorem statement or AC requirement changed.

Connectedness is already part of def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas, clause 1 and its explicit convention. Thus F7 quantifies only over connected surfaces and the proposed disconnected-target counterexample is outside its hypotheses. Independently, exp has derivative exp(z) nonzero and fibre 2pi i Z over 1; open radius-2pi discs isolate its points, so that fibre has no finite subcover while {1} is compact. No repair is needed.

Both centred chart expressions are u^n, so criticality cannot be attributed to a source coordinate at one point and a target coordinate at the other. Replaced that ancillary explanation by coordinate invariance and the common local model. Also corrected 0=f(infinity) to 0=phi_infinity(f(infinity)). The calculation remains degree n, indices n at 0 and infinity and 1 elsewhere, giving -2=-2n+2(n-1), including n=1 with no ramification; inherited AC remains explicit.

repair_notes: Unit 28 completed all ten exact assigned tuple adjudications in the generated dependency order, keeping each item together. Five confirmed fatal defects (three logic, two dependency_citation), three confirmed nonfatal defects and two false positives. Eight item carriers changed; the conic and exponential items stayed unchanged. No new items, workers, judgments, stamps, certificates or round-state changes were made.

Atlas: replaced noncovering-family maximality by maximal completion of a covering holomorphic atlas and proved compatibility locally through a covering chart. Owning contract and manifest now state that covering requirement. Map definition: corrected the C-valued input domain to Omega minus P. Differential: indexed data by connected charts, extended disconnected coefficients componentwise, restricted overlap statements to components, and cleared poles before applying the identity theorem. Order/residue and local chart uses were checked directly.

Planar triangulation: preserved the entire Statement. The finite junction set contains every endpoint of a fixed analytic decomposition, including smooth nonanalytic joins. Direction exclusions and wall heights use that same set. Pairwise disjoint auxiliary-height intervals prevent a band from pinching at both ends. Graph inversion gives one-sided Puiseux expansions; rectangle fans add no extra wall marks, and the pinched cap cut is a full shared edge. The finite avoidance choices do not require AC.

External source actually consulted: Jost, Compact Riemann Surfaces, Theorem 2.3.A.1 proof, printed pp. 37–39, at https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/jost.pdf. Read extracted PDF lines 2069–2152; screenshot attempts failed. This is a geodesic polygon subdivision proof, not a proof of the local slab/Puiseux construction. Corrected the source locator accordingly. The slab argument was verified locally against the four analytic prerequisite statements. No claim is made to have reread Valette or the other references during this review.

Annulus: used a finite radius rho=(r+R)/2 for finite R and rho=r+1 for R=infinity. Pullback: restored target zero order in the final remark, yielding ek+e-1, with equality e-1 only for k=0. Proper degree: read both compact-image suppliers and replaced the metric-only citation/dependency by existing thm-compactness-under-continuous-maps, claim 1 and its open-cover proof. Power map: corrected coordinate-invariance explanation and the target chart value at infinity. No exported Statement changed in these repairs.

False positives: the conic item is an explicit example of C0:x²+y²=1, not a universal classification of conics; its global inverse and transported atlas are valid. The exponential item inherits connectedness from the definition of Riemann surface; the proposed disconnected target is excluded. Its infinite discrete fibre over the compact singleton proves nonproperness.

Necessary owning metadata synchronized under short acquire/reread/edit/check/release sections: research/frontier-36-complete-batch-28.proof-contracts.json, research/frontier-36-complete-proof-contracts.json, and research/frontier-36-complete-batch-28.pages.json. Only assigned entries were updated. Existing independent risk-review records were preserved; these repairs and checks are my own work, not independent review of my repairs.

Every review-contexts call ran immediately after its mathematical review and before the next supplier edit. The recorded hashes were copied from those calls and never refreshed. Subsequent contract-only synchronization does not alter the item guards. No AC requirement or Foundations boundary was weakened.

The three Definition changes have 27 supplier-consumer incidences across 20 distinct direct consumers, all draft frontier items. Exact affected clauses/snippets and sound-use explanations appear in downstream_reviews; downstream is the complete examination inventory, including assigned consumers. No supplier change requires a further consumer edit or transitive expansion. No outside consumer event or published defect was found, so no published-ledger update is proposed.

A separate choice-accounting gap in unassigned lem-finite-analytic-chart-triangulation-compact-riemann-surface step 1.1 is recorded for its frontier owner in ledger_updates. It can be repaired choice-free by covering with all admissible coordinate discs and choosing witnesses only for a finite subcover. No edit to that unassigned carrier was made. This report completes unit 28, not the run-wide owner/maintenance/certification process.

Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with its maximal holomorphic atlas
$\mathcal A$ ([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]). Let
$\mathcal A_c$ be the subatlas of all charts in $\mathcal A$ with nonempty

downstream_reviews.examined_snippet:
The two standard charts $\phi_0(z)=z$ on $\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{\infty\}$
and $\phi_\infty(z)=1/z$ on $\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0\}$, whose
transition on the overlap $\mathbb C^\times$ is $w\mapsto 1/w$, form a
holomorphic atlas on the Riemann sphere; and for every nonempty connected open
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ — in particular $\Omega=\mathbb C$, the unit disc
$\mathbb D=\{z:|z|<1\}$, and every round annulus
$A(0;r,R)=\{z:r<|z|<R\}$ with $0<r<R$ — the single identity chart
$\mathrm{id}:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ is a holomorphic atlas. Each of these examples
satisfies all the Riemann-surface axioms of
[[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]], and the sphere's chart transition
is $1/z$ on $\mathbb C^\times$.
